[Benzinga news, 2026-10-26T10:31:56Z, by staff] Bristol Myers Squibb and SystImmune Announce Positive Phase 3 Results for Izalontamab Brengitecan in NSCLC
Bristol Myers Squibb and partner SystImmune reported positive interim results from the Phase 3 PANKU-Lung01 study, showing that the drug candidate izalontamab brengitecan (Iza-Bren) doubled median progression-free survival in patients with previously-treated EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer.
Bristol Myers Squibb and SystImmune, a subsidiary of Sichuan Biokin Pharmaceutical, announced positive interim analysis results from the Phase 3 PANKU-Lung01 clinical trial. The study evaluated izalontamab brengitecan (Iza-Bren), an EGFRxHER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate, in patients with previously-treated EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Results indicated that the treatment doubled median progression-free survival compared to chemotherapy. Bristol Myers Squibb management highlighted the findings as an important inflection point for the asset, noting its potential to address significant unmet needs across multiple tumor types. The company is currently advancing the development of Iza-Bren as part of its oncology portfolio.
